items.title: learning_scan handler: derive + persist the finding-signals cache
items.context: New handlers/learning-scan.ts: createLearningScanHandlers(ctx) returning { learning_scan(args) }. Call deriveFindingSignalsFromStore(ctx.store, { projectRoot: <the store's project root>, now: <current ISO time> }) so the cache is persisted to .lattice/learning/finding-signals.json via writeFindingSignals. Optional --story restricts storyIds. Render a short summary (signals written, path, updatedAt) and support --json. Reads findings via store ports; the ONLY write is the advisory learning cache; no gate, no finding_add.
items.userSees: Running `lattice learning_scan` derives and writes .lattice/learning/finding-signals.json and prints how many signals were persisted; afterwards review hints can actually fire.
excludes: No referential-staleness filtering at scan time (stays at read time)
No change to the derivation math

happy.desc: Run lattice learning_scan against a store with findings -> .lattice/learning/finding-signals.json is created with valid FindingSignalsCache (schemaVersion, signals[], updatedAt); WHY: proves derive+persist path writes the cache the hint loader reads
Run lattice learning_scan --json -> stdout is parseable JSON with { written: true, path, signals: <n>, updatedAt }; WHY: proves machine-readable output path
Run lattice learning_scan --story <storyId> with a known story -> only signals from that story appear in cache; WHY: proves story-scoping filter works
Run lattice learning_scan (no flags) -> human-readable summary printed to stdout mentioning signal count, path, and updatedAt; WHY: proves default text rendering

edge.desc: Run lattice learning_scan against a store with zero findings -> cache written with signals:[] (empty array), schemaVersion present, no crash; WHY: empty-store boundary
Run lattice learning_scan --story nonexistent-id -> cache written with signals:[] and no error thrown; WHY: non-matching story filter degrades gracefully
Run lattice learning_scan twice with same store state -> output files are byte-identical (deterministic given pinned now); WHY: proves idempotency
Run lattice learning_scan when .lattice/learning/ directory does not yet exist -> directory is created and cache is written; WHY: first-run bootstrap boundary

adversarial.desc: Inspect handler: the ONLY filesystem write is to .lattice/learning/finding-signals.json -- no finding_add, no gate write, no modification to tracked source files; WHY: prevents accidental side-effects that dirty worktree or trip a gate

Pass a projectRoot that differs from the store root (e.g. /tmp/wrong) -> verify cache is still written to correct .lattice/learning/ path relative to actual store, not bogus path; WHY: wrong projectRoot means hint loader never finds cache, defeating the feature

Call learning_scan then verify git status shows no changes to tracked source files (only .lattice/learning/ which is materialHash-excluded); WHY: cache write must not pollute source tree or cause materialHash drift

Invoke learning_scan with unexpected args (--gate, --finding) -> handler ignores or rejects them without side-effects; WHY: ensures handler surface is minimal and cannot be abused to trigger gates/findings

items.title: Register learning_scan as a writing (non-read-only) experience-layer command
items.context: Register in registry.ts (registerBatch(createLearningScanHandlers(ctx))), cli-engine.ts (command entry + schema {json?: boolean, story?: string}), core/config.ts DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS (allow it where appropriate), core/command-policy.ts (a NON-readOnly experience-layer entry: it writes the advisory learning cache; allowedPhases as suitable; cannot satisfy DONE/authority evidence), and core/process-fact-levels.ts PROCESS_FACT_LEVELS (level L2, category 'experience-layer', owner handlers/learning-scan — mirroring signature_registry_set/playbook_propose; required or the process-fact-contract suite fails). Do NOT add it to READ_ONLY_COMMANDS (it writes).
items.userSees: learning_scan is discoverable, correctly classified as a cache-writing experience-layer command, and the full project npm test (incl. process-fact-contract) stays green.

happy.desc: grep registry.ts for registerBatch(createLearningScanHandlers(ctx)) -> learning_scan is batch-registered; WHY: proves command is discoverable via the registry
grep cli-engine.ts for learning_scan command entry with schema {json?: boolean, story?: string} -> entry exists with correct schema; WHY: proves CLI discoverability and argument parsing
grep core/config.ts DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS for learning_scan -> present in appropriate phase groups alongside other experience-layer commands; WHY: proves phase-gating allows the command where needed

grep core/command-policy.ts for learning_scan -> entry exists with ownershipClass that is NOT readOnly, status:supported, destructiveRisk:none; WHY: proves correct policy classification as a writing command

grep core/process-fact-levels.ts PROCESS_FACT_LEVELS for learning_scan -> entry exists with level L2, category experience-layer, owner handlers/learning-scan; WHY: required or process-fact-contract suite fails
Run full npm test -> all pass including process-fact-contract; WHY: proves registration is complete and consistent across all contract checks

edge.desc: Verify learning_scan is NOT present in READ_ONLY_COMMANDS array/set -> absent; WHY: it writes the advisory cache so must not be classified as read-only
Verify learning_scan command-policy allowedPhases does NOT include phases where only read-only commands should run (if such restriction exists); WHY: ensures phase compatibility
Verify learning_scan command-policy entry explicitly notes it cannot satisfy DONE/authority evidence; WHY: prevents misuse as evidence source

adversarial.desc: Temporarily add learning_scan to READ_ONLY_COMMANDS -> run process-fact-contract or command-policy tests -> expect failure (contradiction: writing command in read-only list); WHY: proves the test suite catches this miscategorization
Temporarily remove learning_scan from PROCESS_FACT_LEVELS -> run npm test -> expect process-fact-contract failure; WHY: proves the contract suite enforces completeness

Temporarily set learning_scan ownershipClass to readOnly in command-policy -> run tests -> expect failure or contradiction with the fact it writes .lattice/learning/; WHY: proves policy consistency is enforced

Verify learning_scan is not registered as a gate command and cannot produce gate evidence -> no gate entry in command-policy or gate registry; WHY: prevents accidental gate side-effects from an advisory-only command

items.title: Smoke + npm script + verifier
items.context: New packages/main/src/tasks/experience-layer-learning-scan-smoke.ts: against a temp/real store, run the scan and assert .lattice/learning/finding-signals.json is written with a valid FindingSignalsCache (schemaVersion, signals[] with anchorFiles where present), and that re-running is deterministic. npm script test:experience-layer-learning-scan. Committed verifier verify-<id>.mjs: build clean + this smoke + no-regression smokes + static checks (command registered across cli-engine/registry/config/command-policy/process-fact-levels; NOT in READ_ONLY_COMMANDS; full npm test green) mapping every verificationIntent; prints TOTAL N | PASS N | FAIL 0.
items.userSees: npm smoke passes and the verifier prints PASS for learning_scan.
excludes: No reliance on unrelated repo state

happy.desc: Run npm run test:experience-layer-learning-scan -> smoke passes, prints learning-scan smoke passed; WHY: proves the smoke task executes and validates end-to-end
Smoke asserts .lattice/learning/finding-signals.json is written with valid FindingSignalsCache (schemaVersion present, signals[] array, updatedAt timestamp); WHY: proves cache structural validity

Smoke asserts end-to-end: hint loader returns NO hints before scan (empty/absent cache), then NON-empty hints after scan for a story with matching findings; WHY: proves the product loop activates (addresses product-reviewer advisory)
Run node verify-b-4eb6.mjs -> prints TOTAL N | PASS N | FAIL 0 with all checks green; WHY: proves committed verifier covers all verification intents
Verifier includes full npm test (incl. process-fact-contract) -> green; WHY: proves no regressions from registration

edge.desc: Smoke re-runs scan twice with pinned now -> output cache is byte-identical both times; WHY: proves determinism boundary
Smoke runs against a store with anchorFiles in some signals -> anchorFiles array is present in those signals in the written cache; WHY: proves anchorFiles propagation
Verifier includes no-regression smokes (finding-signals/playbook/recall/revalidation) -> all pass; WHY: proves the new command does not break existing experience-layer functionality

Verifier static checks confirm learning_scan registered across all 5 files (cli-engine, registry, config, command-policy, process-fact-levels) -> all present; WHY: proves registration completeness is machine-verified

adversarial.desc: Verifier confirms learning_scan is NOT in READ_ONLY_COMMANDS -> absent; WHY: machine-enforced check that prevents silent miscategorization after future refactors
Verifier confirms learning_scan ownershipClass is not readOnly -> non-readOnly class found; WHY: machine-enforced policy consistency check

After smoke writes cache, verify git status shows no changes to tracked source files -> only .lattice/learning/ modified (materialHash-excluded); WHY: proves smoke does not pollute the worktree or dirty source
Verifier maps every verificationIntent line to a specific check -> no unmapped intents; WHY: proves the verifier is comprehensive and no intent is silently skipped
Smoke validates that scan with zero findings produces signals:[] not undefined/null/crash -> empty array written; WHY: proves graceful degradation under adversarial empty-state
